EASY DESKTOP FULL GAME 954x621 - the board panel with the six-chip legend beneath it. Chip CHROME is Figma-exact and shipped: 50x50 on a 58px pitch, Green Coal 200 #122524 face, 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.1) border, 8px radius written as a LITERAL because this codebase's rounded-lg is 12px, 3px hard drop shadow per ring, Manrope Bold 14 white centred. ★ THE NUMBERS ARE THE RAIL'S, NOT THE FRAME'S, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: the frame prints 0.5x 0.8x 1.2x 1.5x 2.7x 8.5x; DARTS_RINGS in supabase/functions/_shared/paytables.ts pays 0.2x 0.3x 0.65x 1.55x 3x 8x, and RINGS_MAP in DartsGame.tsx mirrors it. Not one Figma value has ever been paid, so shipping them would be a false payout claim on the page that prints the paytable. tests/gaming/dartsMultiplierLegend.test.ts imports DARTS_RINGS straight from the edge-function module as an INDEPENDENT oracle and pins that none of Figma's six values can reappear.

MEDIUM DESKTOP FULL GAME - same 954x621 panel. ★ THE FRAME'S IMPLIED DIFFICULTY CLAIM IS FALSE AND WAS NOT BUILT: this frame carries a second six-value group inside a HIDDEN vertical frame (9442:16848) that is Easy's six numbers shuffled (0.5x 8.5x 1.5x 0.8x 1.2x 2.7x), which reads as un-updated duplication, not a per-difficulty table. The rail agrees that it should not exist: DARTS_PROBABILITY_WEIGHTS reweights the same seven outcomes per difficulty (easy 36/6/10/19/16/10/3, normal 49/7/8/11/11/9/5, hard 57/7/4/8/10/8/6, ~95% RTP) and the multipliers never move. ONE legend for all three difficulties is therefore correct, and the page ships the caption "Difficulty changes how often each ring lands, not what it pays" directly beneath it.

Each chip is instead pushed from the SETTLEMENT response's own `multiplier` for the ring the throw actually hit, capped at the six the frame draws, newest first, empty until a real throw settles - including 0x misses, which the frame has no chip for but the rail returns more often than any other outcome (36-57% depending on difficulty). Suppressed below lg: the 375/768 board frames (9455-19001, 9467-19582) are 347x347 and draw no such column. ★ ALSO CORRECTING A STALE STILL-OPEN CLAIM: the recorded note that "the in-WIDGET copy of the legend row is still absent" is wrong - DartsGame.tsx renders a legend inside the play area at absolute bottom-6, keyed off RINGS_MAP, i.e. already the rail's six numbers. Shipping the frame's numbers would have been a false payout claim on the very page that prints the paytable. 11 of those 19 rounds paid 0x, i.e. a miss is the single most common outcome (58% observed against the 36-57% the difficulty weights predict), which is why the result column includes 0x chips the frame has none for. The no-mock-data omissions (sample Community-wins rows, 'N playing' counts, 'Total: $89.01') and the dropped 'Try Chicken in Fun Mode' remain standing product rules, not gaps. WARNING - ONE RAIL BEHAVIOUR WORTH A PRODUCT DECISION, reported not patched: POINTS payouts are integers, so the sub-1x rings floor - production shows stake 5 on a 0.3x ring paying 1 (5x0.3=1.5 floored) and stake 1 on a 0.65x ring paying 0. A legend advertising 0.65x that pays nothing on a 1-POINT stake is honest arithmetic but reads as a broken promise at small stakes.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT THIS PASS: it is a new money-path feature rather than a parity correction - it lets the stake GROW between rounds without the player re-confirming, which is responsible-gaming sensitive - and it cannot be exercised on a box with no funded session. EASY DESKTOP IN-PLAY - RE-OPENED 2026-08-20 FOR THE BOARD ITSELF, and the recorded gap ('the populated result column has not been seen') still stands unchanged. NEW AND FIXED THIS PASS: the drawn board was not the board the rail settles. DartsGame.tsx painted five even 8-unit annuli (50/42/34/26/18/8 plus an r=8 bullseye) inside a viewBox '0 0 100 100', while all three settlement paths place the dart at x = 50 + cos(angle)*radius with radius sampled from DARTS_RINGS radiusMin/radiusMax, i.e. 52/42/33/24/15/6/0 in that SAME 0-100 space (the dart is positioned with left: dartX%). Every boundary was off in the same direction, so a dart was drawn one ring too far IN: rail radius 6-8 was paid Ring 1 (3x) and drawn on the GREEN BULLSEYE, 15-18 paid Ring 2 and drawn in red Ring 1, 24-26 paid Ring 3 and drawn in orange Ring 2, 33-34 paid Ring 4 and drawn in yellow Ring 3, and 50-52 paid Outer but fell off the drawn board. Weighted by DARTS_PROBABILITY_WEIGHTS.normal and the radius-uniform sampling, n = 10.4% of throws landed on a colour they were not paid for. Corrected by moving the radii into modules/skai-gaming/src/components/play/games/instant/dartsBoardGeometry.ts, transcribed from DARTS_RINGS, and pinned by dartsBoardGeometry.test.ts, which parses paytables.ts as an INDEPENDENT ORACLE and walks every sampled radius of every payable ring. No payout, odds or settlement code was touched - only the picture of them.

MEDIUM DESKTOP FULL GAME 954x621 - RE-OPENED 2026-09-21. An earlier line closed this node as 'match' on the finding that ONE legend serves all three difficulties. The shipped one-legend design is still right and still ruled, but the premise recorded beside it was not: read live with get_metadata this pass, THE FRAME VARIES BOTH THE PAYTABLE AND THE BOARD GEOMETRY BY DIFFICULTY. Its legend prints 0.2x / 0.5x / 2.5x / 3.6x / 8.8x / 63x where Easy 9411:7933 prints 0.5x / 0.8x / 1.2x / 1.5x / 2.7x / 8.5x, and its rings are 453 / 405.41595 / 386.38232 / 291.21426 / 160.33145 with a 23.79202 bull - fractions 1.0 / 0.894958 / 0.852941 / 0.642857 / 0.353933 / 0.052521 against Easy's 1.0 / 0.894958 / 0.852941 / 0.747899 / 0.411764 / 0.096639. The outer two rims are shared; everything inside them shrinks.
